codeReview.summary: The runtime provider modules already exist and do use GPT-4o-mini plus shared embedding reuse, but this feature run did not actually implement the extraction work described in features.json. Commit 7455b1d only adds tests, and those tests are largely tautological—they never import or execute the provider functions they claim to verify—so the feature was marked complete without real implementation or meaningful validation. There is also still a spec mismatch in advisory prompt construction: context blocks are appended to the user message instead of the system prompt required by the feature description.

issues.description: The new LLM provider tests never import or call `chatCompletion()` or `extractIntent()`; they only assert local literals/helper output (for example `const expectedModel = 'gpt-4o-mini'`). Since commit 7455b1d changes only tests, this feature run provides no real verification for VAL-BE-010/011 or JSON-mode extraction behavior.

The embeddings tests also never import or execute `generateEmbedding()` or the memory/RAG call sites. They assert constants and local mock structures instead, so the claimed single-embedding reuse optimization and OpenAI embedding behavior are not actually validated by this feature commit.

The feature description requires farm, memory, RAG, and attachment context to be injected into the advisory system prompt, but `chatCompletion()` appends `contextBlocks` to the user message (`content: `${input.prompt}${contextPrompt}``) while the system message only contains language and safety instructions.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill's TDD guidance is too loose for Edge Function work: it says to create tests and cover expected behavior, but it does not explicitly require importing/executing the real module under test. That gap allowed this feature to add 1,482 lines of tautological tests and still report `followedProcedure: true`.
